newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians block Gaza road near Jewish settlement.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians block Gaza road near Jewish settlement.

text.p: Hundreds of Palestinian motorists on Sunday clogged a road near a Jewish settlement in the Gaza Strip that Palestinians are not allowed to use, witnesses said.
Israeli military jeeps and armoured personnel carriers took up positions to block the road and officers warned they would open fire if cars pressed on towards the settlement.
The Israeli army said it had made it unequivocally clear that the Palestinians could not block the road and commanders for both sides were in talks to solve the problem.

Palestinian cars veered onto the two-km (one-mile) stretch of road in front of Netzarim settlement after Palestinians blocked Gaza's main highway with metal pipes to force drivers to detour onto the road that passes within 500 metres (yards) of Netzarim.
The road is restricted to use by Jewish settlers, Israeli soldiers and Palestinian police and dignitaries with VIP passes.
"It is a joint road and it should be used by both sides. It has been two years of delays and today we decided that this road should be open," a senior PLO security official told Reuters.
Witnesses said Palestinian police encouraged motorists to travel the road.

A Reuters correspondent said Israeli soldiers had taken up defensive positions in a field next to the road, pointing rifles towards the backed up lines of Palestinian cars. One Israeli border policeman had the words "Born to Kill" written on the back of his police vest.
"If anyone gets closer, to within four metres, of the armoured personnel carrier, we'll shoot him," witnesses quoted an Israeli colonel as telling a Palestinian police major.

The road was closed to all Palestinians in November 1994 when an Islamist suicide bomber on a bicycle blew himself up and killed three soldiers. It was opened to limited Palestinian official traffic in July, and Palestinians said they expected it to be gradually opened to civilian traffic.
"People have no choice but to go the way of Netzarim which is the shortest way, or to go a very long way around," Sufian Abu Zaydeh, head of the Palestinian Authority's Israel desk, told army radio.

Under peace deals that set up Gaza autonomy in 1994, Israeli and Palestinian forces jointly patrol main highways. Israeli troops guard Jewish settlements and roads connected to them. About 4,000 Jewish settlers live amidst Gaza's one million Palestinians.
